items.text: Commit and push the INFO THEORY chapter map and the Ch 1–4 chapter pages
Review the Ch 1–4 chapter pages on the live site and push back on their verdicts
Add the closure identity to the Ch 2 and Ch 4 pages as its own entry
items.detail: Closure at one cut is $I(a;b) = 0 \iff \mathrm{OR} = 1$. The log odds ratio is the pointwise-mutual-information contrast $\mathrm{PMI}_A + \mathrm{PMI}_D - \mathrm{PMI}_B - \mathrm{PMI}_C = -\log(1+\mathrm{nc})$, and $I(a;b)$ is suppressed by the product of the two cut efficiencies. Reword the Ch 2 verdict: mutual information is the closure condition, not a usable closure measure.

items.text: Glossary entries for entropy, mutual information, pointwise mutual information, odds ratio, the data processing inequality and Fano's inequality, linked from the chapter pages
Write the Ch 5 page (differential entropy), then Ch 6 (continuous mutual information)
Check how the Legendre dependence spectrum is defined: orthonormal shifted Legendre polynomials on rank-transformed scores?
items.detail: If so, near independence $I(f_1;f_2) \approx \tfrac12 \sum_{j,k \ge 1} a_{jk}^2$ nats, so the spectrum is already a second-order mutual-information estimate.

items.text: Suppression test: per cut, compute non-closure, $I(a;b)$, distance correlation and the Legendre estimate; plot each global measure against non-closure as the cut efficiencies shrink
items.detail: Confirms that mutual information is blind in the signal-region corner, and tests whether distance correlation and the Legendre spectrum behave the same way (currently a guess).

items.text: Queen write-up: add the mechanism argument for a local closure term on top of a global decorrelation penalty
items.detail: Global dependence measures weight region A by roughly $\varepsilon_a \varepsilon_b$, which would explain the earlier endcap finding that distance correlation stayed flat while non-closure fell. Do not present it as a new metric: the log odds ratio is the standard closure ratio, and both mutual-information decorrelation and a direct non-closure loss are published.
